So `strict=True` errors on: text after closing quote before delimiter (`"b"c`, `"a" ,b`), and unterminated quoted field. My test case `x"y` in an unquoted field is fine (not an error). 

Note: `a,b\rc,d\n` splits into two records — lone \r IS a record separator in the csv module. Per spec "CRLF/LF record endings" but "CSV uses the CPython 3.11 csv.reader default Excel dialect" — the module behavior is normative ✓.

Let me fix the csv-syntax test case to use `"x"y` (quoted then trailing char) which raises "',' expected after '\"'" → capture error. Also add an unterminated-quote case.

Fix the row: `icmp,a,0,1,put,L,1,0/i1,2001:db8:1:100::1,"x"y,echo,,,`

arguments.command:
cd /workspace/tests && python3 - << 'EOF'
src = open('cases.py').read()
src = src.replace("""    # csv syntax error in strict mode: stray quote inside unquoted field
    raw = ','.join(HDR).encode() + b'\\nicmp,a,0,1,put,L,1,0/i1,2001:db8:1:100::1,x"y,echo,,,\\n'
    bad('csv-syntax', {'encoding': 'csv', 'chunks': [b64(raw)]})""",
"""    # csv syntax errors in strict mode: junk after closing quote / unterminated
    raw = ','.join(HDR).encode() + b'\\nicmp,a,0,1,put,L,1,0/i1,2001:db8:1:100::1,"x"y,echo,,,\\n'
    bad('csv-syntax', {'encoding': 'csv', 'chunks': [b64(raw)]})
    raw = ','.join(HDR).encode() + b'\\nicmp,a,0,1,put,L,1,0/i1,2001:db8:1:100::1,"x,echo,,,\\n'
    bad('csv-unterminated', {'encoding': 'csv', 'chunks': [b64(raw)]})""")
open('cases.py','w').write(src)
EOF
cd /workspace && timeout 600 python3 tests/cases.py
